terms.gloss: move, stir; make an impression on
evidence: Traupman 100: maximē commoveō, make a deep impression on
terms.comment: To move someone’s mind; in itself neutral, whether to fear, pity or admiration, so the context or an ablative says which (see affect).

terms.gloss: impress someone, fill someone with admiration
evidence: Nep. Iph. 3: cuivīs injicere admīrātiōnem suī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Also admīrātiōnem movēre (Cic. Phil. 10.2: hoc mihi maximam admīrātiōnem movet). To be impressed by something is simply to admire it: mīror, admīror.

terms.gloss: win approval for, make (something) acceptable to someone
evidence: Cic. Att. 4.14.1: quōs (librōs), ut spērō, tibi valdē probābō (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Sē probāre alicui is to win someone’s good opinion, to make a good impression: multīs sē probāvit (Cic. Fin. 2.81, of Epicurus).

phrases.english: this amazes me more than anything

sources: Lewis & Short: commoveo · Lewis & Short: admiratio · Lewis & Short: probo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 100, checked against the searchable text of the book.
